{"body": "## What & Why\n\n`ElasticsearchDB.get()` wrapped the client call and response parsing in one `try` whose blanket `except Exception` returned `None` for everything \u2014 including connection refusals, auth failures and cluster outages. `None` is what every caller reads as \"no such vector\", so a backend outage looked like missing data. The codebase already documents the opposite contract: `_update_memory()` in `mem0/memory/main.py` wraps `vector_store.get()` in `except Exception: ... raise` with the comment *\"Backing-store failure, not a bad memory_id: re-raise the original so the REST layer maps it to 5xx, not 4xx\"*. The `update()` path is worse: `None` there inserts a duplicate row where the user asked for an update (#7516).\n\nFix: split `get()` into two phases \u2014\n\n- `NotFoundError` from the client call (a missing document, the only genuine \"no such vector\") returns `None`;\n- every other client-call failure logs and re-raises;\n- response parse-shape failures (`KeyError`/`TypeError` on `_id`/`_source`) keep degrading to `None`.\n\n## Tests\n\n- `test_get_not_found` now uses the real `NotFoundError` (it previously pinned the bug with a generic `Exception(\"Not found\")` \u2192 `None`).\n- New `test_get_transport_error_propagates`: a `ConnectionError` propagates (verified red on the old code).\n- New `test_get_malformed_response_returns_none`: missing `_source` and a `None` response still degrade to `None`.\n\nFull `tests/vector_stores/test_elasticsearch.py`: 24 passed (Python 3.12, elasticsearch 8.19.3). `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean.\n\nFixes #7516"}
